jigStages.title: 1. THE BARE BENCH
jigStages.see: One flat sheet on sawhorses, and nothing else. This board is the only thing in the whole build that has to be true.
jigStages.does: Flatness. Every angle below is measured from this one surface, so the panel cannot wind or twist as long as the board does not.

jigStages.title: 2. THE TRIANGLE, DRAWN ONCE
jigStages.see: The panel's mathematical triangle, snapped onto the board. It is drawn one time, from the geodesic solution, and never measured again.
jigStages.does: Repeatability. Forty panels are laid out from three lines that were struck once, instead of from forty tape measurements.

jigStages.title: 3. AXIS RAILS
jigStages.see: Three low cleats, one per member, each set parallel to that member's point-axis and just to the seam side of it.
jigStages.does: Position across the panel. Push the stick against its rail and the sector's point line sits exactly where the solution says. The rail references the sawn point, never the bark, so a lumpy log does not move the joint.

jigStages.title: 4. RED / GREEN ORIENTATION FENCES
jigStages.see: Two short cradle plates per member, standing against the two sawn radial faces of the wedge.
jigStages.does: Rotation about the stick's own axis. A 45-degree sector dropped in rotated 90 or 180 degrees still LOOKS fine; these plates make it not fit. Red side to red plate, green side to green plate, or the stick does not seat.

jigStages.title: 5. THE TWO CUT PLANES
jigStages.see: The magenta plate at each head end is the flush-cut fence. The cyan plate is the receiving face the next stick's butt will land on.
jigStages.does: The saw. A circular saw or a handsaw run flat against the magenta face cuts the head to the exact plane of the triangle edge, without anyone setting a bevel or a mitre angle.

jigStages.title: 6. THE BUTT CUT, MADE OFF THE JIG
jigStages.see: One stick, still full length at both ends, laid up to the cyan plate. The amber tail past that plate is the stock the butt cut removes.
jigStages.does: Batching. This is the ONLY cut made before assembly, and every stick of the same family takes the same one, so it can be run through a saw bench in a batch rather than fitted one at a time.

jigStages.title: 7. FIRST STICK ON THE BENCH
jigStages.see: The same stick, butt now cut, dropped against its rail and its two fences. The head end is still long and hangs off the board.
jigStages.does: Two ends, two different operations. The butt arrives finished; the head arrives long on purpose and is not touched yet.

jigStages.title: 8. SECOND STICK, BUTT ONTO SIDE
jigStages.see: The second stick lands so that the FIRST stick's butt bears on its radial face -- on the side of it, not on its end.
jigStages.does: End-to-side. Nothing is mitred to meet at a point; the joint is a flat sawn face pressed onto a flat sawn face, which is what a split wedge already has without any further machining.

jigStages.title: 9. THE LAST STICK SLIDES IN
jigStages.see: The third stick is captured at BOTH ends once the other two are down, so it cannot drop in from above. It is shown backed off along its own axis, ready to slide home into the pocket.
jigStages.does: The chain is cyclic. This is the one awkward move in the whole method, and it is why the head end is left long: the extra length is what gives the last stick somewhere to come from.

jigStages.title: 10. PULLED UP TIGHT
jigStages.see: Home. Three butts bearing on three sides, the green outlines are the actual contact faces, and all three heads still hang off long.
jigStages.does: Self-locating. With the loop closed the frame holds its own shape and the jig is only keeping it flat while the heads are trimmed.

jigStages.title: 11. FLUSH-CUT THE THREE HEADS
jigStages.see: Each head is sawn back to its magenta fence. The orange stock hanging past the board is what falls off.
jigStages.does: This is the whole trick. The head is never measured. It is cut in place, to the plane the neighbouring member has already established, so error in stock length or in the butt angle leaves as offcut instead of accumulating around the triangle.

jigStages.title: 12. PANEL OFF THE JIG
jigStages.see: A finished triangular frame, its three corners clean inside the mathematical triangle. The jig is empty and unchanged.
jigStages.does: Forty of these come off the same fixture. Nothing on the jig was adjusted between panels, so panel forty is panel one.
